workflow.budget: Maximum amount in US dollars for one run. Every request reserves its highest possible cost in advance, so parallel steps cannot exceed the budget together. Empty = default budget from the settings.
workflow.limits: Limits how many steps of a run work at the same time, how long a run may actively work and how many steps it runs in total. At the time limit, running steps are cancelled; a request already sent still finishes.
workflow.contract: The fields the workflow promises as its result. If the result does not fit, the run fails instead of passing on something unchecked.
workflow.capabilities: Tags for what the workflow can do as a team. They help to find a fitting team and grant no permissions.
workflow.problems: These points prevent the start. They are checked again after every change.
workflow.import: Loads an exported workflow file (.nodestro.json) as a new copy. Existing workflows stay unchanged.
workflow.export: Saves the workflow with all agent settings as a JSON file. Knowledge files, memory and your own tools are not included.
workflow.duplicate: Creates a copy of the workflow; executions are not copied.
workflow.start: Saves the workflow and opens the start dialog. Locked while problems are open or a run is active.
workflow.save: Saves all changes (Ctrl+S). The workflow is also saved automatically before every start.
workflow.addAgent: Adds an empty agent to the right of the last node.
workflow.autoLayout: Arranges all nodes from left to right in the order of their data flow.
workflow.palette: Drag building blocks onto the canvas or click them. Templates from the agent library appear below.
workflow.paletteDesign: Describe in your own words what an agent should do. The Agent Architect proposes a complete configuration; this costs one request to the AI provider.
workflow.startNode: The input given at start flows to all agents connected to the start. A workflow does not need a start node; agents without predecessors receive the input as well.
workflow.defaultInput: This text is already in the input field when starting and can be changed there.
workflow.outputNode: Collects the results of the connected agents. Without a result node, the output of the last agents is the result.
workflow.runInput: Goes to all agents that are connected to the start or have no predecessors. In tasks it is available everywhere as {{runInput}}.
workflow.runFiles: For this run only, these knowledge files are placed directly into the context of the first agents (the agents at the start).
workflow.runBudget: The workflow's budget or, if empty, the default budget from the settings.
workflow.discard: Discards all unsaved changes including undo/redo and loads the last saved state.
workflow.versions: Every save is a version with a date. Older versions can be viewed and restored without losing any.
workflow.organize: Favorites come first; tags help with filtering.
workflow.loop: A loop connection leads from a branch of a decision or approval back to an earlier step. The steps in between run again until the branch is no longer taken or the limit is reached.

agent.design: From your description, the Agent Architect designs role, system prompt, model, effort and tools. You review the proposal before it is applied.
agent.saveTemplate: Saves a copy of this configuration in the agent library. It then appears in the palette of every workflow.
agent.model: Provider and model of this agent. Pick a model from the list or type any model id of the provider. Larger models think more thoroughly but cost more per token.
agent.systemPrompt: Lasting instructions for the agent: role, approach, style and quality standard. Applies to every task of this agent.
agent.task: The concrete task per run. {{input}} inserts the results of the predecessors, {{runInput}} the workflow's input, {{agentName}} the result of a specific predecessor.
agent.placeholders: Inserts the placeholder of a direct predecessor. Predecessor results that are not used are appended under “# Inputs”.
agent.tools: Functions the agent can call by itself. It decides from the tool description when a call helps.
agent.serverTools: Tools that Anthropic runs on its servers. Web search costs an extra $10 per 1,000 searches.
agent.knowledge: Files from “Knowledge” that this agent may use. It only sees the files assigned here.
agent.knowledgeMode: In context: files are always in the prompt. On demand: the agent loads files itself (tool “files”). Search: the agent looks for matching passages (tool “search”).
agent.citations: In “In context” mode, answers point to the exact passages in the documents (in “Search” mode, sources are always included). Cannot be combined with a structured output format.
agent.memory: A notebook of text files under /memories that the agent reads and maintains itself.
agent.memorySpace: The named storage location for persistent memory. Agents with the same space share their notes.
agent.memoryAssistant: An assistant proposes a file structure with initial content. It is saved only after you confirm.
agent.output: Text returns Markdown. Structured (JSON) returns a validated object with fixed fields; successors receive it as JSON.
agent.outputFieldName: Key in the JSON result. Letters, digits and _ only, not starting with a digit, e.g. summary or key_metrics.
agent.outputFieldType: Data type of the field. The result is checked against this type.
agent.outputFieldDescription: Tells the model what belongs in this field. The more precise, the better the result.
agent.outputFieldRequired: Required fields must always be filled. Optional fields may be missing (null).
agent.effort: How thoroughly the model works. Higher effort means more thinking, more tokens and higher costs, but often better results.
agent.thinking: Adaptive: the model thinks when it helps. “Only between tool calls” exists only for Sonnet 5.5 up to effort “High”. Not all models support “Off”.
agent.thinkingDisplay: Whether and how the model's reasoning appears in the execution. Cannot be combined with thinking “Off” or “Only between tool calls”.
agent.quality: A second model (judge) checks the result against your criteria. If it fails, the agent revises its answer. Every check costs additional tokens.
agent.qualityCriterion: A criterion with name and description. The judge rates each criterion separately as passed/failed with a reason.
agent.qualityRevisions: How many times at most the agent may revise after a failed check (0–5).
agent.judgeModel: The model that performs the check. A strong model judges more reliably.
agent.maxTokens: Maximum number of output tokens per answer (thinking included). If it is too small, the answer stops with an error.
agent.maxToolRounds: How many rounds of tool calls an agent may make at most per task. After that, the agent ends with an error.
agent.parallelTools: How many tool calls of one answer run at the same time. 1 = one after another.
agent.toolChoice: Automatic: the model decides. No tools: it only answers. Forcing a tool is not possible with Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1.
agent.toolErrors: On: the agent sees unexpected tool errors as a result and can react. Off: such an error ends the agent.
agent.caching: Repeated parts of the prompt (system prompt, tools, knowledge) are cached and then read at a much lower price. The first write costs a little more.
agent.cacheTtl: How long the cache stays valid. 1 hour pays off when runs come less often than every 5 minutes; writing is more expensive then.
agent.refusal: If the model refuses a request for safety reasons: treat it as an error or keep the (usually empty) answer text.
agent.fallbacks: If the model refuses, the API answers the request with the next model in this list. Sonnet 5.5 does not support its own list.
agent.examples: Example dialogues before the actual task (few-shot). They show the model the format you want. Must start with the user and end with the assistant.
agent.requestOptions: For advanced users: additional fields added unchanged to every API request. Must be a JSON object.
agent.test: Runs only this agent with a test input and shows answer, tools, tokens and cost. Uses API credit, but is not a workflow run.
agent.preview: Shows what the agent gets in the next run: system prompt, task with inserted inputs and further context. No API call.
agent.paletteDesign: Describe in your own words what an agent should do. The Agent Architect proposes a complete configuration; this costs one request to the assistant model.

tools.kind: Built-in: ships with Nodestro. Your own tool: written by you. AI-created: written by the Coding Agent and approved by you.
tools.schema: Describes the parameters the agent passes when calling. It is generated from the function's types and docstring.
tools.try: Runs the tool with the JSON input, exactly as an agent would. Your own tools run in the sandbox; there are no API costs.
tools.delete: Withdraws the tool. Agents that have it assigned cannot start until you remove it from them.
tools.functionName: Name of the Python function in the code. It becomes the tool name agents see.
tools.tests: test_* functions that check the tool with assert (from tool import …). Nothing is saved without passing tests.
tools.check: Checks the code statically and runs the tests in the sandbox, without saving.
tools.save: Checks and saves the tool. If the name already exists, a new version replaces the old one.
tools.generate: A Coding Agent writes the function and tests (up to three attempts). Only after your approval is the tool available to all agents. Costs API tokens.
tools.approve: Approved tools can be used by all agents. Check beforehand that code and tests do what you expect. Without a decision, a job is rejected after one hour.
tools.sandbox: Your own and AI-created tools never run in the Nodestro process, but isolated with time and memory limits.
tools.drafts: Tools written by the Workflow Architect. Test and approve them here, or reject them.
tools.services: External services through MCP: you connect a server, test the connection and approve each tool after reviewing it. When the service changes a tool, it is blocked until you review the change.
tools.callApproval: A person decides about each call of this tool, with the exact arguments. Without a decision within the time limit, the call counts as rejected.
tools.servicesLocal: A local MCP server runs in an isolated container. Its packages are reviewed and approved like a tool's libraries.
tools.servicesOAuth: Some services require a sign-in. Nodestro opens their sign-in page and keeps the access encrypted.

knowledge.upload: PDFs, images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) and text formats. Images up to 5 MB, documents up to 20 MB. Texts and PDFs are indexed for search.
knowledge.description: Helps agents in “On demand” mode decide which file to load. Saved when you leave the field.
knowledge.chunks: The file was split into sections of about 1,500 characters for full-text search (PDFs page by page). Without sections it cannot be searched.
knowledge.search: Full-text search (BM25) over all indexed files – this is how an agent in “Search” mode finds matching passages. Costs nothing.
knowledge.score: Relevance of the hit: the higher, the better the section matches the search.
knowledge.collections: Collections group knowledge files, e.g. “Contracts” or “Product data”. Agents still get exactly the files assigned to them.

memory.space: A memory space is a file system of its own under /memories. Agents with “Persistent” memory and this space read and write here.
memory.clear: Permanently deletes all files of the space. Agents start without memories afterwards.
memory.newFile: Creates an empty file under /memories, e.g. customers/preferences.md. Agents find it on the next run.

runs.importTrace: Opens an exported trace file (run_….json) for viewing. Nothing is run, there are no costs, and existing executions stay unchanged.
runs.exportTrace: Saves the complete run as JSON: workflow, input, results, tool calls, errors, times, tokens and costs.
runs.imported: This run was imported from a trace file. It is only displayed and does not count towards the usage of this installation.
runs.cancel: Cancels the run. Running agents stop at the next step; tokens already used are charged.
runs.requests: Number of requests to the AI provider's API. Every tool round and every quality check is a request of its own.
runs.tokens: Sum of input, output and cache tokens. Thoughts (thinking) count as output tokens.
runs.cost: Estimate based on list prices, including cache and web search. “–” means: at least one request could not be priced.
runs.trace: Timeline: each bar shows when an agent ran. Bars on top of each other ran in parallel. Click an agent for details.
runs.evaluation: Result of the judge's quality check: passed or not, number of attempts and the reason for each criterion.
runs.exportSanitized: Replaces credentials and, if you want, personal data or whole contents in the exported copy.
runs.compare: Select two runs to see result, agents, models, tokens, cost and evaluations side by side.

usage.period: Time span over which runs are added up (by start time).
usage.byModel: Usage per agent model. The quality check counts towards the model of the agent being checked.
usage.share: Share of the estimated total costs of the period.
usage.sources: Besides workflow runs, agent tests, agent design, the memory assistant and tool creation use tokens too. Every request is counted exactly once.

settings.defaultModel: New, empty agents and new workflows start with this model. For AI drafts it serves as a replacement if the proposed model is not available.
settings.assistantModel: Model for the Agent Architect, the Coding Agent and the memory assistant. A strong model makes better proposals.
settings.budget: Applies to all workflows without a budget of their own. Empty = no limit (not recommended).
settings.sandbox: Python process: for tools you wrote yourself, with time and memory limits. Built-in Linux sandbox (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13): AI-created tools run there automatically, without network and without access to your files, keys or other programs. Docker: a container, also without network and with a read-only file system.
settings.language: The language of the interface. “Automatic” follows the browser's language (English if it is not supported). The choice takes effect at once and is remembered. Content such as agents, prompts and results stays as it is.
settings.backup: Downloads all data except the API keys as a ZIP file.
settings.restore: Checks the file completely first and shows its contents. Data is only replaced after your confirmation; the current state is backed up before.
settings.diagnostics: Checks versions, database, directories, sandbox and requirements. Free and without internet.
settings.connection: Asks the provider of the default model for its list of models. Uses no tokens.
settings.architectBudget: Maximum estimated cost of one Workflow Architect draft. The architect stops when it is reached.
settings.architectRepairs: Limits the extra AI requests for corrections. Obvious fixes are made without AI.
settings.providers: Access to the AI providers: API keys (never shown; environment variables take precedence), base URLs of your own servers and what their models can do. Every agent uses the provider of its model; nothing switches to another provider.
settings.prices: Where the prices come from, how often they are checked, and how individual prices and reviews work.
settings.priceMode: Standard warns about unknown and stale prices; Strict refuses such requests before they cost anything.
settings.reconciliation: Compares the estimates with the providers' bills. Needs an admin key of the billing API; nothing is changed.

search.global: Searches workflows, agents, tools, knowledge and documentation (Ctrl+K).

library.copy: Creates your own, independent workflow in the chosen language and opens it in the editor. The template stays unchanged, and no model is called.
library.language: The language in which the copy's names, prompts and test task are created. It defaults to the interface language; a saved copy does not change with it later.
library.sensitive: Finance, law, HR or administration: the agents point out uncertainties but do not replace professional advice. A qualified person must check the results.
library.synthetic: All test data is invented and marked as synthetic. Replace it with your own data in the start node.
library.sequential: The agents work one after another; each builds on the result of the one before.
library.parallel: Several agents work on the same input at the same time; another agent combines their results.
library.branching: The workflow branches by rules or after an approval; not every agent always runs.

architect.open: Let the Workflow Architect design a new workflow or revise this one from a description. You review the draft before anything changes.
architect.create: Describe the goal; the architect plans, configures and checks a complete workflow.
architect.generateTools: If no existing tool fits, the Coding Agent writes a Python tool as a draft. It only runs after your explicit approval.
architect.log: Every line describes a step the architect actually carried out or a result it got. Internal reasoning of the model is not shown.
architect.cost: Estimated API cost of all requests of this draft so far. It is recorded in the usage overview under Workflow Architect.
architect.cancel: Stops at once. Nothing is saved, no workflow changes; requests already sent are counted.
architect.assumptions: Details your description left open, which the architect decided. Check that they fit.
architect.validation: The same check as before a run: structure, connections, placeholders and every agent configuration.
architect.toolDraft: A tool draft is code and tests that were only checked statically. Approve it to register it for all agents.
architect.toolTest: Runs the tests in the sandbox. The tool is not registered.
architect.toolApprove: Your approval: the tests run in the sandbox, and only if all pass the tool is registered. Its calls always run in the sandbox.
architect.acceptCreate: Creates the workflow and opens it. It does not run; start it yourself when you are ready.
architect.applyRevision: Applies the changes in the editor as one step. Undo takes them back; nothing is saved until you save.
architect.saveFirst: Saves your current, unsaved state as a version before the changes are applied.

python.workflow: Third-party libraries the tools of this workflow need. Each workflow has its own environment and its own approvals.
python.tool: For the tests of a tool with libraries Nodestro creates a separate test environment. It is only installed after your approval.
python.architect: The architect detects libraries in new tools but installs nothing. You approve them when testing and in the workflow.
python.maintenance: All managed Python environments with size and owner. Deleted environments are reinstalled from the approved versions when needed.
python.cleanup: Removes environments whose workflow or tool no longer exists, and downloads that are no longer needed.

assistant.open: The Nodestro Assistant answers questions from the documentation and discusses objects you attach. It never changes anything itself. Shortcut: Ctrl+J.
assistant.discuss: Attaches this object to the assistant chat. Only then does the assistant get its content; secrets are replaced first.
assistant.attach: Choose workflows, agents, tools, memory, knowledge or runs as context. Memory and knowledge content is only included if you explicitly select it.
assistant.suggestion: A suggestion from the current view. It is not sent until you add it.
assistant.draft: Sends the editor's current, not yet saved state instead of the saved version.
assistant.refresh: Uses the current state for the following messages. Earlier messages keep the state they were sent with.
assistant.handover: Opens the existing function with this proposal. You start and review it there; nothing changes before that.
assistant.cost: Estimated API cost at list price. Every request appears exactly once on the usage page under Nodestro Assistant.
assistant.history: All chats: continue, rename or delete them. They are stored locally in the Nodestro database and are part of the backup.

flow.condition: A decision checks a result with fixed rules (no AI) and opens the matching branches. Branches not chosen are skipped.
flow.conditionSource: Which result is checked. Empty: the result that arrives through the connection.
flow.conditionRules: Every rule is a branch with its own output. A rule compares a field of the result with a value.
flow.conditionMode: First matching rule: exactly one branch. All matching rules: several branches may run at the same time.
flow.conditionInvalid: When the field is missing or has the wrong type, the decision takes the otherwise branch or fails.
flow.approval: The run pauses until a person approves or rejects. Open approvals are listed under Approvals.
flow.approvalShow: The reviewer sees these results. Nothing selected: everything that arrives here.
flow.approvalReject: When rejected, the run follows the “Rejected” branch or ends as cancelled.
flow.approvals: Every run that waits for a human decision.
flow.subworkflow: Runs another workflow as one step. Its result arrives here like an agent's.
flow.subworkflowVersion: A fixed version protects against later changes to the sub-workflow.
flow.subworkflowValues: Values for the sub-workflow's input form; placeholders are allowed.
flow.form: Fields asked for and checked at the start. Agents read them with {{formName}}.
flow.formField: The technical name is used in the placeholder: letters, digits and _ only.
flow.resume: Continues a failed run: valid results are taken over, the rest runs again.
flow.resumeSideEffects: Steps that run again had called tools. A second call may trigger something twice.
flow.orchestrator: An AI model plans the task and delegates parts of it to teams of its pool, one decision at a time. Every decision is recorded with its reason.
flow.orchestratorTeams: Teams are saved workflows. The model only sees their name, description, capabilities and output contract. It cannot add teams.
flow.orchestratorLimits: The limits keep an orchestrator from running in circles: it stops after the maximum number of decisions, and the workflow's budget and limits apply as well.
flow.orchestratorSelect: Instead of naming every team, name capabilities. When a run starts, saved teams that share them are added to the pool and fixed for that run; the run's details show which tags each team matched. Nothing is scored: more matching tags come first, then the name.

files.output: Formats in which the result node stores its result at the end of the run: Markdown, JSON, CSV, HTML or PDF.
files.sanitize: Replaces credentials and personal data in the file with placeholders.
files.run: Files of this run. HTML is shown without scripts.
files.formats: Word (DOCX) and Excel (XLSX) are converted to Markdown on upload; formulas are shown, never run.
files.ocr: Scanned PDFs without a text layer can be recognised locally with Tesseract. Uncertain words are marked.

automation.batch: One workflow over many inputs. Every row becomes a run of its own.
automation.batchMapping: Map every column to a field of the input form or to the free input.
automation.batchLimits: Limits stop the batch before it gets too expensive or fails too often.
automation.concurrency: More parallel runs are faster but may hit the API's rate limits.
automation.benchmark: Fixed test cases that make changes to the workflow measurable.
automation.benchmarkChecks: Rules check the result without AI, e.g. “category equals complaint”.
automation.benchmarkJudge: An AI rates the result by your criteria. Its verdict is marked as an AI rating and costs extra.
automation.benchmarkCompare: Pick two test runs to see case by case what got better or worse.
automation.benchmarkModels: Test the same cases with other models for single agents, then compare the two test runs. The workflow itself does not change.
automation.schedule: Starts a workflow regularly while Nodestro runs.
automation.scheduleMissed: When Nodestro was off at the time: skip it, or catch up once at the next start.
automation.scheduleTimeZone: Times apply in this time zone, including daylight saving time.
automation.estimate: Estimated from the latest successful runs of this workflow. The maximum follows from the budget per run.
automation.external: Own tools may e.g. send messages. With many runs this happens just as often.
automation.caseFromRun: Turns this failed run's input into a test case, with credentials and personal data replaced. Nothing is saved until you confirm.

publish.open: Publish this workflow as an API on this computer, manage keys and network access, or export it as a standalone FastAPI project.
publish.publish: Freezes the saved version with its tools and sub-workflows. Later edits do not change it until you publish again.
publish.note: A short note for yourself, e.g. what changed in this version.
publish.slug: The name of the API in its URL: /api/published/<name>/runs.
publish.rollback: Makes this version the one /runs uses again. Nothing is republished; running runs keep their version.
publish.disable: Refuses new runs with 503 until you switch the API on again.
publish.keyName: Who uses the key, e.g. the name of the application. Only shown in Nodestro.
publish.scopes: run starts and cancels runs, read reads status and results, approve decides approvals.
publish.network: Opens a separate port for devices in your network. Off by default; the Nodestro interface is never reachable there.
publish.networkShare: Only APIs switched on here are reachable through the network port.
publish.validate: Checks the request body exactly like the API does. No run starts, nothing is billed.
publish.testRun: Starts a real run of the published version through the API's own path; it is billed like any run.
publish.sync: Lets clients wait for the result in one request (?wait=<seconds>), up to the time limit.
publish.library: How the exported project gets Orkexa: from its Git repository, or as included source code (MIT license).
publish.export: Generates the project as a ZIP: runtime, workflow version, tests, examples and README. Nothing is sent anywhere.
publish.gate: Requires a current test result before every new version. Mandatory checks always block; weaker results can be released with a reason.
publish.gateOverride: The reason is stored with the version and in the API's history. Mandatory checks can never be skipped.
publish.mcpTool: Lets MCP clients on this computer start this API as a tool. Off by default; the operator must also switch it on.

inputs.field: Files for this run: upload, drop or choose from knowledge. They are checked and stored for the run only, not in knowledge.
inputs.config: Set whether the field takes one or several files, and how many at most.
inputs.formats: Choose groups or single formats. Nodestro checks the real content, not only the extension.
inputs.optional: Required fields must be filled before the start. Optional fields may stay empty; agents and decisions notice that.
inputs.delivery: How agents get the files: as content, as an overview with targeted reading, or automatically depending on the size.
inputs.storage: Uploaded files are kept with the runs. Clean up unused and old files here.
inputs.adopt: Stores chosen content permanently in knowledge, only after your confirmation and with its origin.
inputs.proposals: The agent may propose content for knowledge. Only what you check and confirm is stored.
inputs.received: Which files the run got and how each agent received them.
